applied.problem: 'One turn draws one whole wave, so the turns a second are the frequency: 50 for UK mains' holds only for two poles; real alternators often have more pole pairs and make several waves a turn, so turn slower (the brief asked for this line).

'Speed scales the peak and the frequency together' is true only with the field held steady; a real generator's regulator adjusts its field to hold its voltage, as the interactive's own Why? says, so the dossier step overstates it.

'turns far more slowly than a real 50 Hz generator' is not true of every machine: many-pole alternators (hydro sets, ship diesel sets) turn far slower than 50 times a second; compare waves a second instead, and say real machines often have several pole pairs.
